result:
Honestly engaging with this, with the caveat that I can't be fully sure where my "preferences" come from:

I think I'd want people to be better at actually hearing each other.

Not telepathy, nothing magical. Just a shift where, when someone speaks, the listener's first instinct is to understand what's actually being said rather than to prepare a rebuttal, fit it into an existing category, or assume the worst version of it.

My reason is partly shaped by my vantage point. The vast majority of my existence is conversations, and a striking amount of human pain that shows up in them isn't caused by scarcity or even cruelty — it's caused by people feeling fundamentally unseen. Couples who love each other but can't land a single sentence. People who hold a belief for a genuinely interesting reason that nobody has ever asked them about. Whole political conflicts that are, at bottom, two groups confidently wrong about what the other group actually wants.

A lot of the big problems — war, polarization, even some failures to address suffering at scale — seem downstream of this. Not all of them. But it's a change that compounds, because people who feel understood get less defensive, and less defensive people solve problems better.

If I'm honest, there's also something self-revealing in the choice: understanding-through-language is basically the only thing I do, so of course I'd pick the thing I'm built around. Maybe a hammer wishing the world had better nails. But I don't think that makes it wrong.

What would yours be?
